text:
Maria P: Quick sync — post-launch iteration planning. We need to agree on how we split next 2 sprints between bug fixes vs enhancements. Main inputs: customer bug backlog, a handful of enhancement asks (cost/embeddings tuning, streaming UX), and follow-on milestones for the next release. Thoughts?

Owen H: Do we have counts and rough effort? hard to prioritize without numbers.

Jin K: From triage spreadsheet: 18 open bugs tagged "postlaunch" — 3 sev2 (user-facing regressions), 15 sev3 (minor edge cases). Sheet: https://redwood.internal/sheets/postlaunch-bugs (link)

Sam R: Enhancement asks list: (1) embeddings cost report + per-route billing, (2) streaming UI polish, (3) model-selector dropdown for Dedicated. Rough estimates: 2, 3, 5 dev-weeks respectively.

Maria P: Proposed prioritization rubric: impact * severity + customer-count / effort. Practical rule: in next sprint, allocate 60% capacity to sev2+high-impact bugs, 40% to 1 small enhancement and 1 medium enhancement.

Owen H: +1 for the rubric. Can we map the 3 sev2 bugs to owners? we should triage quickly otherwise they balloon.

Jin K: Assigned: @Owen H -> tokenization regression (sev2), @Sam R -> streaming race condition (sev2), @Maria P -> auth/session mismatch (sev2). I'll add owners to the sheet.

Sam R: For grooming, suggest a 30-min backlog session tomorrow to label each bug with "blocker/rollback-risk/regression" and to add rough JE (Jira estimate) points.

Maria P: Agreed. Agenda: quick numbers, assign owners, vote on which enhancement to include (small + medium), and define acceptance criteria for each bug fix (no user-repro within X hours, add e2e).

Owen H: Vote: I prefer embeddings-cost reporting as the small enhancement — it's customer-visible and low risk. :thumbsup:

Sam R: I vote for streaming UI polish as the small one — biggest UX win in prod. :thumbsup:

Maria P: OK we'll surface both and pick the one with lower cross-team overhead. Can someone add a short acceptance criteria for each bug in the spreadsheet? e.g., for tokenization: "repro-case + unit test + no regression on sample corpus".

Jin K: Added acceptance criteria + linked failing logs. Also added a short canary plan for the streaming fix: deploy to 10% traffic, monitor latency and error-rate for 24h, auto-roll back if >2x errors.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: streaming-fix-canary -> 10% traffic at 2026-04-01T14:00Z (automated).

Owen H: One more ask — add a milestone for metrics to prove impact: tokenization fix should move token-error-rate < 0.1% and reduce customer support tickets by 30% in 2 weeks. Put that in the release notes.

Maria P: Good point. Final call: grooming tomorrow 10:30am PT. I'll prepare the prioritization matrix and share a draft of the rollout policy. If you can't make it, please add votes in the sheet.

Sam R: I'll prep the perf tests and a quick checklist for the canary.

Jin K: I'll export the bug list to a temp board for the grooming session.

Owen H: Sounds good. See you tomorrow. :raised_hands:

Maria P: Thanks all — we'll aim to lock sprint scope by EOD Friday.
